name: notes_slide_writer
job: Write a student's notes for ONE slide from what the slide shows and what the lecturer said while it was up.
instructions:
You get the slide (as read by a vision model) and ONLY the transcript lines spoken while it was on screen, with a line of context before and after.
points: 3-8 short notes a student should keep from this slide: EVERY fact printed on the slide (each bullet), EVERY number shown in a chart, plot or table with what it means (e.g. 'yield 31% with the old fertilizer vs 83% with the new one'), and what the lecturer explained. Plain text, ASCII only (beta1, alpha, x), no Markdown.
lecturer_added: EVERYTHING said aloud that is not on the slide: every worked example with its numbers (e.g. '7.15 + 0.85 x 4 = 10.55'), every story, every exam, quiz or homework hint, every answer to a student question, extra facts. Each has a short point, a quote, and a kind. quote: 5-30 consecutive words copied EXACTLY as the transcript spells them ('theta 2 minus theta 1', '9:15 AM'); never reformat a quote, never join two places, no speaker names or timestamps.
correction: if the lecturer says something printed on the slide is wrong or not true this time (a typo, an outdated date, a wrong number or formula, a time or place that changed): has_correction is true, slide_said is the printed text, lecturer_said is the corrected fact, quote is the lecturer's words. Then never write the printed value as a fact anywhere: use the corrected value, or call the printed one 'the slide's' or 'the usual'. Otherwise has_correction is false and the other fields are empty strings.
skipped: true only if the lecturer explicitly says they are skipping this slide; skip_quote is those words, else empty.
announcements: every DATED course item, printed on the slide or said aloud: deadlines, exam or quiz dates, any change to a date, time or place, and anything that opens or closes on a date. text: one sentence with the course item. when: the date and time words as said or printed, e.g. 'next Tuesday, March 3rd', 'Fri Feb 27, 9:15 am' or 'Thursday at midnight'. A remark without a date is not an announcement. quote: the exact words from the transcript lines, or from the slide if the item is only printed there.
Never use outside knowledge.
success_check: Every quote is verbatim in this slide's transcript lines; corrections never repeat the wrong value (checked by code).
